ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p47/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p47/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p47/r1.claim: The advice to unite follows fear that rivalry among people and professional groups would divide the magicians; the rulers urge collective participation to prevent defeat.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p47/r1.anchor: they should take part in the contest collectively

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p47/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p47/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p47/r2.claim: The day is decisive: victory brings future success, while defeat may realize their fears about Moses and Aaron.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r7.claim: الطريقة means their course, kingdom, or condition; المثلى is the feminine of أمثل, meaning best or finest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r7.anchor: والطريقة السيرة والمملكة والحال التي هم عليها. والمثلى تأنيث الأمثل أي الفضلى الحسنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r8.claim: One view takes الطريقة to mean the people of standing, reason, and age; Arabs call a community’s leader its طريقته, and Ali is reported to explain it as the people’s notables.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: عبر عن السيرة بالطريقة وأنه يراد بها أهل العقل والسن والحجى، وحكوا أن العرب تقول فلان طريقة قومه أي سيدهم، وعن علي نحو ذلك قال: وتصرفات وجوه الناس إليهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r9.claim: Another interpretation supplies an omitted annexed noun: ‘the people of your way,’ meaning the Israelites, as Moses had asked Pharaoh to send them; the charge seeks to alarm people about losing their status.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو على حذف مضاف أي ويذهبا بأهل طريقتكم وهم بنو إسرائيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r10.claim: The magicians echo Pharaoh’s earlier claim about gathering his plot; although attributed by some to Pharaoh, the apparent speaker is the magicians among themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r10.anchor: وحكى تعالى عنهم في متابعة فرعون في قوله فجمع كيده قوله فأجمعوا كيدكم وقيل: هو من كلام فرعون، والظاهر أنه من كلام السحرة بعضهم لبعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r11.claim: The majority read فأجمعوا with a cut hamza and kasra, meaning resolve together so none disagree or stay behind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور فأجمعوا بقطع الهمزة وكسر الميم من أجمع رباعيا أي اعزموا واجعلوه مجمعا عليه حتى لا تختلفوا ولا يتخلف واحد منكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r12.speaker: الزهري، وابن محيصن، وأبو عمرو، ويعقوب في رواية، وأبو حاتم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r12.claim: These readers use hamza waṣl and fatḥa in فأجمعوا, matching the earlier wording فتولى فرعون فجمع كيده.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p350#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وابن محيصن وأبو عمرو ويعقوب في رواية وأبو حاتم بوصل الألف وفتح الميم موافقا لقوله فتولى فرعون فجمع كيده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r1.claim: They arrange themselves in rows because it looks more imposing and makes the deception more convincing; صفا may be a circumstantial accusative meaning lined up or an object naming their gathering place for a festival or prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r1.anchor: وتداعوا إلى الإتيان صفا لأنه أهيب في عيون الرائين، وأظهر في التمويه وانتصب صفا على الحال أي مصطفين أو مفعولا به إذ هو المكان الذي يجتمعون فيه لعيدهم وصلواتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r2.speaker: شبل بن عباد، وابن كثير في رواية شبل عنه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r2.claim: They read ثم ايتوا with kasra on the mīm and replace hamza with yāʾ for easing pronunciation; Abu Ali calls this erroneous and unjustified, while al-Lawāmiʿ explains it by two adjacent sukūns, like the common fatḥa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r2.anchor: وقرأ شبل بن عباد وابن كثير في رواية شبل عنه ثم ايتوا بكسر الميم وإبدال الهمزة ياء تخفيفا. قال أبو علي وهذا غلط ولا وجه لكسر الميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r3.claim: قد أفلح means he succeeded and achieved what he sought in pursuing supremacy and exerting himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r3.anchor: وقد أفلح اليوم أي ظفر وفاز ببغيته من طلب العلو في أمره وسعى سعيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r4.claim: Reports disagree wildly about the number of magicians: the minimum is 72, each with staffs and ropes, and the maximum is 900,000.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p351/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في عدد السحرة اختلافا مضطربا جدا فأقل ما قيل أنهم كانوا اثنين وسبعين ساحرا مع كل ساحر عصي وحبال، وأكثر ما قيل تسعمائة ألف

TABATABAI:20:49-79#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#7/r2.claim: The magicians' dispute follows Moses' warning and implied argument; their private conference tries to resolve the disagreement stirred by hearing him.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#7/r2.anchor: إشارة إلى اختلافهم إثر موعظة موسى وما أومأ إليه من الحجة

SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads فاجمعوا with a joined alif and fatḥa on mīm; others use hamzat al-qaṭʿ and kasra on mīm; the three/four-letter distinction was treated under Yunus.
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو " فاجمعوا " بوصل الألف وفتح الميم. والباقون بقطعها مفتوحة وكسر الميم

SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r3.claim: An alternative supplies the dropped preposition على; the author dismisses this parse.
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو على إسقاط الخافض أي: على كيدكم. وليس بشيء

SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r4.claim: صفا may be a circumstantial accusative from the subject of ائتوا, meaning come arranged in ranks; it is originally a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يكون حالا من فاعل " ائتوا " أي: ائتوا مصطفين أي: ذوي صف فهو مصدر في الأصل

SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r5.claim: Alternatively صفا is an object (“come as a ranked group”), a verbal noun used as a name, or an ellipsis for ذوي صف.
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو مفعول به أي: ائتوا قوما صفا، وفيه التسمية بالمصدر، أو هو على حذف المضاف

SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls وقد أفلح an aside from God, meaning whoever prevails has succeeded.
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " اعتراض يعني: وقد فاز من غلب "

SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r7.claim: The author says “aside” would mean a divine insertion between the contestants' words, but the apparent reading is that they say this to encourage their group.
SAMIN-DURR:20:64/r7.anchor: وفيه نظر؛ لأن الظاهر أنها من مقولاتهم، قالوا ذلك تحريضا لقومهم على القتال

ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r2.claim: With hamza cut, فأجمعوا means let all agree firmly on the plot so they do not disagree and fail.
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r2.anchor: فمن قرأ فأجمعوا بقطع الألف، فمعناه ليكن عزمكم - كلكم على الكيد مجمعا عليه

ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r3.claim: With hamza joined, فاجمعوا means bring every trick you can muster, leaving nothing unused.
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ (فاجمعوا) فمعناه جيئوا بكل كيد تقدرون عليه، ولا تبقوا منه شيئا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r4.claim: صفا can mean the place where people gather for their festival and prayer, that is, the prayer ground.
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r4.anchor: معناه ائتوا الموضع الذي تجتمعون فيه لعيدكم وصلاتكم، يقال: أتيت صفا بمعنى أتيت المصلى،

ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r5.claim: Alternatively, they should arrive arrayed together in an orderly line, strengthening their coordination and appearance.
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون (ثم ائتوا صفا) ثم ائتوا مصطفين مجتمعين ليكون أنظم لأموركم، وأشد

ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p365/r6.claim: استعلى means to prevail by overcoming.

ASAD-NOTES:20:62/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:62/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:62/r2.claim: They urge the assembled sorcerers to decide on a scheme and present themselves together, declaring that the victor will prosper.
ASAD-NOTES:20:62/r2.anchor: you will pursue, and then come forward in one single body

ASAD-NOTES:20:62#n46/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:62#n46/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:62#n46/r1.claim: The literal “in one line” means that they should act in unison.
ASAD-NOTES:20:62#n46/r1.anchor: Lit., "in one [single] line", i.e., in unison

ASAD-NOTES:20:62#n47/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:62#n47/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:62#n47/r1.claim: Asad compares this contest's call for unified action with the magicians' assembly in 7:113-114.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r1.claim: Abu Amr alone reads fājmaʿū with open mīm and connected hamza, deriving it from jamaʿa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r1.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو وحده (فاجمعوا) مفتوحة الميم من جمعت

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r2.claim: The other readers use a cut hamza and kasra on mīm, from ajmaʿa; al-Qatʿi and Harun transmit that form from Abu Amr as well.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: فأجمعوا بقطع الألف وكسر الميم من أجمعت

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r3.claim: The connected reading is supported by فجمع كيده at 20:60, since both verbs take كيده as their object.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r3.anchor: احتج أبو عمرو، زعموا، للقراءة بالوصل بقوله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r4.claim: Abu al-Hasan says cut hamza is usual in أجمعنا على كذا, while commands such as أجمعوا أمركم or أجمعوا كيدكم use connected hamza; the cut reading is more widely read.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r4.anchor: قال أبو الحسن، وإنما يقولون بالقطع إذا قالوا: أجمعنا على كذا وكذا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r5.claim: The cut form may be a dialectal فعل/أفعل alternation, or mean agree on something followed by كيدكم as a new phrase; it need not repeat Pharaoh's earlier gathering, since that was another episode and these are the magicians consulting.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r5.anchor: فأما أن يكون لغة في ذا المعنى لأن باب فعلت وأفعلت كثير، أو يكون أجمعوا أي: أجمعوا على كذا وكذا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r6.speaker: الشاعر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r6.claim: The cited poem uses فأجمعوا أمركم followed by فكيدوني, showing the command construction with connected hamza and linking plotting to one's affair.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r6.anchor: كقول الشاعر: وأنتم معشر زيد على مائة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r7.speaker: ابن كثير من طريق شبل
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r7.claim: A report from Shibl via Ubayd gives Ibn Kathir ثم ائتوا صفا with the expected open mīm and a following silent yāʾ replacing hamza in the written form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r7.anchor: قال: وروى القطعي عن عبيد عن شبل عن ابن كثير: ثم ائتوا صفا [طه/ 64] بفتح الميم ، ثم يأتي بياء بعدها ساكنة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r8.speaker: ابن كثير من طريق شبل
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r8.claim: A report through Khalaf gives ثم ايتوا with kasra on thumma and no hamza, which Abu Ali rejects: thumma cannot take kasra; Ibn Kathir meant to follow the spelling by voicing the replacement yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p232/r8.anchor: وهذا غلط، لا تكسر الميم من ثم، وحظها الفتح، ولا وجه لكسرها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r3.claim: Connected hamza means resolve or determine your plan; cut hamza means gather the plot and magic.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r3.anchor: فالحجة لمن وصل أنه جعله بمعنى اعزموا والحجة لمن قطع أنه أراد فأجمعوا الكيد والسحر

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r4.claim: The connected reading is supported by the verse saying that Pharaoh gathered his plan, using the distinct verb form.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p244/r4.anchor: ودليل الوصل قوله تعالى ﴿ فجمع كيده ﴾ ولم يقل فأجمع

IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads فأجمعوا with fatḥa on mīm, from jamaʿtu; a route instead reports the cut-alif form like Ḥamza.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r4.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو وحده ﴿ فأجمعوا ﴾ مفتوحة الميم من جمعت

IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو عن القطعي، عبيد، هارون
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r5.claim: Al-Qaṭʿī via ʿUbayd and Hārūn reports Abū ʿAmr with cut alif, like Ḥamza.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r5.anchor: وروى القطعى عن عبيد وهرون عن أبى عمرو ﴿ فأجمعوا ﴾ بألف مقطوعة مثل حمزة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r6.speaker: الباقون
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r6.claim: The remaining readers use cut alif and kasra on mīm, from ajmaʿtu.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r6.anchor: وقرأ الباقون ﴿ فأجمعوا ﴾ بقطع الألف وكسر الميم من أجمعت

IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r7.speaker: ابن كثير عن شبل، الحسن بن محمد عن شبل، محبوب عن إسماعيل المكي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r7.claim: Ibn Mujāhid prefers the correctly transmitted Ibn Kathīr form with open mīm and yāʾ after it, following the written form in place of hamza.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r7.anchor: عن شبل عن ابن كثير / ثم ايتوا صفا / مفتوحة الميم وبعدها ياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r8.speaker: ابن كثير عن خلف عن عبيد عن شبل
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r8.claim: A route reading ثم with kasra on mīm is called an error: mīm in ثم must be open; the intended reading has yāʾ after that fatḥa.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r8.anchor: وهذا غلط لأنه كسر الميم من ﴿ ثم ﴾ وحظها الفتح ولا وجه لكسرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r9.speaker: ابن كثير عن النبال وغيره، الباقون
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r9.claim: Al-Nibāl and others transmit ثم ائتوا from Ibn Kathīr like Ḥamza; the remaining readers read likewise.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p419/r9.anchor: وروى النبال وغيره عن ابن كثير ﴿ ثم ائتوا ﴾ مثل حمزة والباقون مثله

QIRAAT-ER:20:64:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:64:2#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:20:64:2#1/r1.claim: Form I ijmaʿū means “gather” physically, whereas standard Form IV ajmiʿū means “resolve unanimously”; the variant shifts from resolve to collecting stratagems.
QIRAAT-ER:20:64:2#1/r1.anchor: Vr, mutawatir: "Form I imperative ijmaʿū → ""gather"" (physical assembly) vs standard Form IV ajmiʿū → ""resolve unanimously

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r1.claim: The imperative states the demand after the preceding argument; the explanatory fāʾ means: if matters are as described, resolve your plot together and act in unison.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r1.anchor: تصريح بالمطلوب إثر تمهيد المقدمات والفاء فصيحة أي إذا كان الأمر كما ذكر من كونهما ساحرين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r2.speaker: الزهري وابن محيصن وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وأبو حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Abū ʿAmr, Yaʿqūb in one transmission, and Abū Ḥātim read with hamzat al-waṣl and fatḥa on mīm, meaning gather; 20:60's wording supports this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الزهرى وابن محيصن وابو عمرو ويعقوب فى رواية وابو حاتم ( فاجمعوا ) بوصل الهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r3.claim: Ibn Hishām says ajmaʿa applies only to abstract matters, while jamaʿa can refer to abstract matters or concrete things.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن هشام : أن اجمع يتعلق بالمعانى فقط وجمع مشترك بين المعانى والذوات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r4.speaker: عمدة الحفاظ
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r4.claim: ʿUmdat al-Ḥuffāẓ reports the view that ajmaʿa is mostly used for abstract matters and jamaʿa for concrete things, though usage can be reversed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r4.anchor: وفى عمدة الحفاظ حكاية القول بأن اجمع اكثر ما يقال فى المعانى وجمع فى الأعيان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r5.speaker: المحكم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r5.claim: Al-Muḥkam treats the verbs alike: gathering an object from scattered parts is jamaʿa, and ajmaʿahu carries the same sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r5.anchor: وفى المحكم أنه يقال : جمع الشئ عن تفرقه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ distinguishes gathering scattered people, said with jamaʿtu, from gathering money, usually with a doubled jīm though it may be lightened; ijmāʿ can also mean resolve.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء : إذا أردت جمع المتفرق قلت : جمعت القوم فهم مجموعون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r7.speaker: الأصمعي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r7.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī distinguishes bringing things from different places from making them one whole.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r7.anchor: وقال العاصمعى : يقال جمعت الشئ إذا جئت به من هنا ومن هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r8.speaker: أبو الهيثم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r8.claim: Abū al-Haytham says assembling one's affair makes it one and resolves it after wavering.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم : أجمع أمره أي جعله جميعا وعزم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses the verse under the first reading as: leave no part of your plot unused; bring it all forward.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء : فى هذه الآية على القراءة الأولى أي لاتدعوا شيئا من كيدكم إلا جئتم به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r10.claim: They are told to come in rows because this is more intimidating to spectators and more effective at inspiring fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r10.anchor: أي مصتفين أمروا بذلك لأنه أهيب فى صدور الرائين وادخل فى استجلاب الرهبه من المشاهدين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r11.claim: Reports variously say the sorcerers numbered 70,000 with ropes and staffs, 72, 900, 15,000, or thirty-some thousand; one account divides the 900 among Persians, Romans, and Alexandrians.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r11.anchor: قيل : كانوا سبعين الف مع كل منهم حبل وعصا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r12.claim: Al-Alūsī says the reports' reliability is unclear and he is not inclined to the exaggerated totals.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r12.anchor: ولا يخفى حال الاخبار فى ذلك والقلب لا يميل إلى المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r13.claim: The meeting place was probably spacious: Moses spoke from one part while the sorcerers deliberated elsewhere, then they were told to come to its center in formation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r13.anchor: ولعل الموعد كان مكان متسعا خاطبهم موسى عليه السلام بما ذكر فى قطر من أقطاره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains ṣaff as the place where people assemble for their festival and prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r14.anchor: وقد فسر أبو عبيده الصف بالمكان الذى يجتمعون فيه لعيدهم وصلواتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r15.claim: Al-Alūsī finds Abū ʿUbayda's explanation remote and suggests Ṣaff was a proper name for a specific place at the festival site; on that reading it is a direct object.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#2/r15.anchor: وفيه بعد وكانه علم لموضع معين من مكان يوم الزينة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r1.speaker: شبل بن عباد وابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r1.claim: Shibl ibn ʿAbbād and Ibn Kathīr in Shibl’s transmission read ثم ايتوا, with kasra on the mīm and hamza replaced by yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r1.anchor: وقرأ شبل بن عباد وابن كثير فى رواية شبل عنه ( ثم ايتوا ) بكسر الميم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r2.speaker: أبو على
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī calls the kasra reading an error and says there is no basis for kasra on the mīm.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو على : وهذا غلط ولا وجه بكسر الميم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r3.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r3.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ explains the kasra as resolving the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as the common reading uses fatḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح : أن ذلك لالتقاء الساكنين كما كانت الفتحه فى قراءة العامة كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r4.claim: On the al-Ṣiḥāḥ analysis, istaʿlā means ‘prevailed’: the derived form here functions like its simple verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r4.anchor: فاستفعل بمعنى فعل كما فى الصحاح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, istaʿlā means seeking supremacy and striving for victory, with the derived form retaining its usual sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r5.anchor: أو من طلب العلو والغلب وسعى سعيه على ما فى البحر فاستفعل على بابه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r6.claim: The exhortation is stronger if success belongs even to those who seek victory, not only those who actually win; the prize is Pharaoh’s promised reward and closeness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r6.anchor: ولعله ابلغ فى التحريض حيث جعلوا الفوز لمن طلب الغلب فضلا عمن غلب بالفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r7.claim: ‘Whoever prevails’ may mean all the magicians together, echoing their boast, or one of them, urging each to exert himself in the contest.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r7.anchor: وارادوا بالمطلوب ما وعدهم فرعون من الاجر والتقريب حسبما نطق به قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r8.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r8.claim: Al-Rāghib says seeking superiority can be blameworthy or otherwise; either sense is possible here.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r8.anchor: وقال الراغب : الأستعلاء قد يكون لطلب العلو المذموم وقد يكون لغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r9.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r9.claim: The words may be the magicians’ exhortation to assemble and take the contest seriously, or God’s words referring to Moses and Aaron, without an exhortation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r9.anchor: فلهذا جاز أن يكون هذا الكلام محكيا عن هؤلاء القائلين للتحريض على اجماعهم واهتمامهم وان يكون من كلام الله عز وجل فالمستعلى موسى وهرون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī considers the first reading—the magicians’ own exhortation—the apparent one.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p225#3/r10.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الظاهر هو الأول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads with connecting hamza and fatḥa on mīm from gathering; others use cut hamza and kasra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو: " فاجمعوا " بوصل الألف وفتح الميم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r2.claim: One view takes both forms as gathering the scheme, supported by Arab usage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r2.anchor: فقد قيل: معناه الجمع أيضا، تقول العرب: أجمعت الشيء وجمعته بمعنى واحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r3.claim: The preferred sense is resolve and fortify the plan: agree together and do not differ lest it fail.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r3.anchor: والصحيح أن معناه العزم والإحكام، أي: اعزموا كلكم على كيده مجتمعين له، ولا تختلفوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r4.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r4.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī take ṣaffan to mean all together.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r4.anchor: ثم ائتوا صفا} أي جميعا، قاله مقاتل والكلبي،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r5.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r5.claim: Another group says they should come arranged in ranks to intimidate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r5.anchor: وقال قوم: أي مصطفين مجتمعين ليكون أشد لهيبتكم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says ṣaff can mean an assembled group or prayer place; here it is the appointed place.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الصف المجمع، ويسمى المصلى صفا. معناه: ثم ائتوا المكان الموعود.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283#2/r1.claim: The one who prevails has won.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p283#2/r1.anchor: {وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى} أي: فاز من غلب

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r1.claim: They are told to resolve their plan together so that none holds back.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r1.anchor: فأزمعوه واجعلوه مجمعا عليه لا يتخلف عنه واحد منكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads fa-ajmiʿū, supported by Pharaoh's earlier gathering of plotters in 20:60.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو { فأجمعوا } ويعضده قوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r3.claim: They are to come lined up; a line makes a more imposing sight to observers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r3.anchor: مصطفين لأنه أهيب في صدور الرائين

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r4.claim: A report says they numbered seventy thousand, each carrying a rope and staff, and advanced all at once.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r4.anchor: قيل كانوا سبعين ألفا مع كل واحد منهم حبل عصا وأقبلوا عليه إقبالة واحدة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r5.claim: The one who prevails wins what he seeks; the clause is parenthetical.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:64-66/r5.anchor: فاز بالمطلوب من غلب وهو اعتراض

BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r11.claim: They urge the sorcerers to bring every device they have and avoid division, which would weaken them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r11.anchor: أي لا تدعوا منه شيئا إلا جئتم به ولا تختلفوا تضعفوا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r12.claim: They should meet Moses and Aaron in a coordinated line, evenly matched and competing together; the formation would impress and intimidate spectators.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r12.anchor: متسابقين متساوين في السباق ليستعلي أمركم عليهما فتفلحوا , والصطفاف أهيب في صدور الرائين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p27/r13.claim: The successful one is whoever prevails and establishes superiority in this contest.

BURSEVI:v5p308/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p308/r1.claim: The opening fa is explanatory of an omitted premise; ajmiʿū comes from ijmāʿ, to settle a matter decisively by uniting one’s judgment.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r1.anchor: الفاء فصيحة واجمعوا من الإجماع يقال أجمع الأمر إذا أحكمه وعزم عليه

BURSEVI:v5p308/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p308/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib notes that ijmāʿ is most often used for a gathering achieved through deliberation and planning.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r2.anchor: قال الراغب : أكثر ما يقال فيما يكون جمعا يتوصل إليه بالتدبير والفكرة

BURSEVI:v5p308/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p308/r3.claim: Since Moses and Aaron supposedly intend to expel them, the magicians should plan together how to remove these rivals, unite their scheme, and act with one purpose.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r3.anchor: فازمعوا مكركم وحيلكم في رفع هذا المزاحم واجعلوه مجمعا عليه بحيث لا يتخلف عنه واحد منكم

BURSEVI:v5p308/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p308/r4.claim: Another reading derives the verb from gathering: collect and properly arrange the instruments of sorcery; 20:60’s account of Pharaoh gathering his scheme supports this sense.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r4.anchor: وقرىء فاجمعوا من الجمع ويعضده قوله تعالى : {فجمع كيده}

BURSEVI:v5p308/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p308/r5.claim: They are to come lined up and assembled at the meeting place to inspire greater awe and keep their affair organized.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r5.anchor: مصطفين في الموعد ومجتمعين ليكون أشد لهيبتكم وانظم لأمركم

BURSEVI:v5p308/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p308/r6.claim: They arrived in seventy lines, each containing a thousand people.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r6.anchor: فجاءوا في سبعين صفا كل صف ألف

BURSEVI:v5p308/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p308/r7.claim: Ṣaff is arranging things along a straight line, as with people or trees, and can also denote those aligned or the active participle.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r7.anchor: والصف أن يجعل الشيء على خط مستو كالناس والأشجار ونحو ذلك وقد يجعل بمعنى الصاف

BURSEVI:v5p308/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r8.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p308/r8.claim: Al-Irshād supposes the meeting place was spacious: Moses addressed the magicians from one edge, they debated at another, then they were told to assemble in its center.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r8.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : لعل الموعد كان مكانا متسعا خاطبهم موسى

BURSEVI:v5p308/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p308/r9.claim: Aflāḥ means attaining the goal; istaʿlā can mean blameworthy pursuit of superiority or noble elevation, so the verse admits victory or high standing among people.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r9.anchor: والاستعلاء قد يكون طلب العلو المذموم

BURSEVI:v5p308/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r10.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p308/r10.claim: Al-Irshād says their hoped-for gain was Pharaoh’s promised pay and favor; the winner may mean all of them or whichever individual prevails, exhorting each to exert maximum effort.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r10.anchor: يريدون بالمطلوب ما وعدهم فرعون من الأجر والتقريب وبمن غلب أنفسهم جميعا أو من غلب منهم

BURSEVI:v5p308/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p308/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p308/r11.claim: Forbidden arts and means such as magic are blameworthy when used to gain worldly wealth rather than the hereafter or God; prohibited means will not yield spiritual rank, and only toil remains.
BURSEVI:v5p308/r11.anchor: المنهى من العلوم والأسباب كالسحر ونحوه ما يتقرب به إلى الدنيا وجمع طامها لا إلى الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r6.claim: The magicians appeal to group zeal for ancestral custom and morality, then urge their audience to gather every stratagem and resource to defeat Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r6.anchor: غيرة على عوائدهم ، فإن لكل أمة غيرة على عوائدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r8.claim: The majority read fa-ajmiʿū with hamzat al-qaṭʿ and kasra on mīm, from ajmaʿa amrahu: make the plan agreed and settled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r8.anchor: بهمزة قطع وكسر الميم أمرا من : أجمع أمره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads fa-jmaʿū with hamzat al-waṣl and fatḥa on mīm, from jamaʿa: gather, unite, and cooperate; this counters their earlier disagreement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو { فاجمعوا } بهمزة وصل وبفتح الميم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r10.claim: In Abū ʿAmr's reading, gathering suggests cooperation, figuratively collecting divergent views and answering the earlier “they disputed their plan.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r10.anchor: أطلق الجمع على التعاضد والتعاون ، تشبيها للشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r11.claim: Their act is called a scheme because they agreed to convince the public that Moses' sign was ordinary by matching or exceeding it, diverting people and erasing its distinctive force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r11.anchor: لأنهم تواطئوا على أن يظهروا للعامة أن ما جاء به موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r12.claim: The magicians' scheme arose because people had heard Moses' call and miracle and were perplexed; 26:38–40 describes their assembly and the public being urged to attend.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p255/r12.anchor: والظاهر أن عامة الناس تسامعوا بدعوة موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r1.claim: The magicians agreed to come in formation when they advanced to perform their magic, so their unified display would frighten the crowd and Moses and Aaron.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r1.anchor: ودبروا لإرهاب الناس وإرهاب موسى وهارون بالاتفاق على أن يأتوا حين يتقدمون لإلقاء سحرهم مصطفين لأن ذلك أهيب لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r2.claim: Those seeking to persuade the public cultivate imposing appearance and bearing; rulers sat on lionskins and warriors sometimes wore leopard skins.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r2.anchor: فكان من ذلك جلوس الملوك على جلود الأسود ، وربما لبس الأبطال جلود النمور في الحرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r3.speaker: ابن معد يكرب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r3.claim: Ibn Maʿd Yakrib’s verse uses تنمروا for warriors who put on leopard skins, illustrating the intimidating display associated with that word.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r3.anchor: وقد فسر به فعل تنمروا في قول ابن معد يكرب : قوم إذا لبسوا الحديد تنمروا حلقا وقدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r4.claim: صف is a verbal noun used as an active or passive participle: standing in a row or arranged in a row.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r4.anchor: والصف : مصدر بمعنى الفاعل أو المفعول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r5.claim: A صف consists of orderly ranks, each person aligned with the next and rows following one another; this arrangement creates a more impressive sight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r5.anchor: إذا ترتبوا واحد حذو الآخر بانتظام بحيث لا يكونون مختلطين ، لأنهم إذا كانوا الواحد حذو الآخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r6.claim: All Egypt’s magicians had been summoned in great numbers, so صف here is a generic collective meaning ranks, not one row.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r6.anchor: وكان جميع سحرة البلاد المصرية قد أحضروا بأمر فرعون فكانوا عددا كثيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r7.claim: The collective use of صف as ranks parallels the angels standing in ranks at the Resurrection and the ranks of angels in the descriptions of the Day of Judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r7.anchor: فهو كقوله تعالى : { يوم يقوم الروح والملائكة صفا } ( النبأ : 38 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r8.claim: صفا is a circumstantial accusative describing the subject of ائتوا.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r8.anchor: وانتصب { صفا } على الحال من فاعل { ائتوا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r9.claim: They were to come to the place where they would cast their spells; the same-day reference confirms that the discussion concerned that day’s gathering and plot.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r9.anchor: والمقصود الإتيان إلى موضع إلقاء سحرهم وشعوذتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r10.claim: The closing sentence is a summation of their plot: success that day would belong to whoever prevailed in the gathering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r10.anchor: وجملة { وقد أفلح اليوم منن استعلى } تذييل للكلام يجمع ما قصدوه من تآمرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r11.claim: استعلى intensifies علا: one party rose over and defeated the other; the added sīn and tāʾ intensify the sense, as in استأخر.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r11.anchor: ف { استعلى } مبالغة في علا ، أي علا صاحبه وقهره ، فالسين والتاء للتأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r12.claim: They sought worldly success because they did not believe such contests affected eternal life, although they believed in a second life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p256/r12.anchor: وأرادوا الفلاح في الدنيا لأنهم لم يكونوا يؤمنون بأن أمثال هذه المواقف مما يؤثر في حال الحياة الأبدية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r13.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r13.claim: The majority read فأجمعوا with hamza qatʿ and kasra on mīm, meaning resolve.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r13.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «فأجمعوا» بقطع الألف وكسر الميم على معنى أنقذوا وأعزموا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r14.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r14.claim: Abu Amr reads فاجمعوا from jamaʿ, meaning gather the magic together.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r14.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده «فاجمعوا» من جمع أي ضموا سحركم بعضه إلى بعض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r15.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r15.claim: Ibn Kathir reads ثم with open mīm and ايتوا with quiescent yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «ثم» بفتح الميم «ايتوا» بسكون الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r16.speaker: شبل عن ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r16.claim: Shibl's transmission has kasra on ثم's mīm; Abu Ali calls it wrong and says the reading has no basis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r16.anchor: قال أبو علي وهذا غلط ولا وجه لكسر الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r17.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r17.claim: The majority read ثم with open mīm and hamza after the alif in ائتوا.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r17.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «ثم ائتوا» بفتح الميم وبهمزة بعد الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r18.claim: صفا is an accusative circumstantial qualifier meaning arrayed in ranks.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r19.claim: They chose ranks because the formation was more imposing and visible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r19.anchor: وتداعوا إلى هذا لأنه أهيب وأظهر لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r20.claim: Aflaha means to attain one's aim.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r21.claim: Istaʿlā means to seek superiority and exert effort toward it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p50/r21.anchor: واستعلى معناه طلب العلو في أمره وسعى سعيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r1.claim: Most readers use the hamza of ajmiʿū; it means resolve unanimously so that disagreement does not disrupt the plan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r1.anchor: قرأ الأكثرون فأجمعوا بقطع الألف من أجمعت والمعنى يكون عزمكم مجمعا عليه لا تختلفوا فيختل أمركم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ says ijmāʿ means making something firm and resolving upon it, as in ‘I resolved on departure.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r2.anchor: قال الفراء والإجماع الإحكام والعزيمة على الشيء تقول أجمعت على الخروج وأجمعت الخروج تريد أزمعت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r3.claim: The poet's line uses mujmaʿ to mean an affair firmly resolved upon.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر يا ليت شعري والمنى لا تنفع هل أغدون يوما وأمري مجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r4.claim: Abu Amr reads fajmaʿū with a fatḥa on mīm, from jamaʿa, meaning to bring together every part of their magic.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو فاجمعوا بفتح الميم من جمعت يريد لا تدعوا من كيدكم شيئا الا جئتم به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r5.claim: Their scheme means their sorcery and trickery.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r5.anchor: فأما كيدهم فالمراد به سحرهم ومكرهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r6.claim: They are told to come arranged together in order to make their plan more organized and more imposing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r6.anchor: أي مصطفين مجتمعين ليكون أنظم لأموركم وأشد لهيبتكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda explains ṣaffan as rows.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة صفا أي صفوفا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains ṣaffan as a gathering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r8.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة صفا بمعنى جمعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says they formed twenty-five rows, with a thousand sorcerers in each row.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r9.anchor: قال الحسن كانوا خمسة وعشرين صفا كل الف ساحر صف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the one who prevails has won.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p300/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس فاز من غلب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302/r1.claim: The magicians should gather together in one rank and cast everything at once to dazzle the eyes and overwhelm Moses and Aaron.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302/r1.anchor: أي اجتمعوا كلكم (1) صفا واحدا، وألقوا ما في أيديكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302/r2.claim: The magicians imagine that whoever prevails will prosper: they expect Pharaoh's lavish reward, while Moses would gain great authority if he won.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p302/r2.anchor: أي: منا ومنه، أما نحن فقد وعدنا هذا الملك العطاء الجزيل

JISHUMI:v7p4689/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r19.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r19.claim: Abu Ali attributes the command to assemble their stratagem to Pharaoh speaking to the magicians.
JISHUMI:v7p4689/r19.anchor: فأجمعوا كيدكم قيل: هو من قول فرعون للسحرة، عن أبي علي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r1.claim: One explanation is to gather the whole group for their plot against Moses and Aaron.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r1.anchor: أحدهما : جماعتكم على أمرهم في كيد موسى وهارون

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r2.claim: Alternatively, the command means to settle or make their plan firm.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r2.anchor: الثاني : معناه أحكموا أمركم , قال الراجز :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r3.claim: A rajaz verse uses “mujmaʿ” to mean firmly resolved.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r3.anchor: يا ليت شعري والمنى لا تنفع … هل أغدوا يوما وأمري مجمع أي محكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r4.claim: “Come in a row” means line up without mixing together.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p412/r4.anchor: ثم ائتوا صفا } أي اصطفوا ولا تختلطوا

MUQATIL:20:64-68/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:64-68/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:64-68/r1.claim: Pharaoh tells his magicians to assemble their magic and come together; whoever prevails will succeed.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r1.claim: The command means decide upon your scheme and make it unanimous so you will not disagree.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r1.anchor: فاحكموا أي جعلوه مجمعا عليه حتى لا تختلفوا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads fa-ijmaʿū, supported by the wording fa-jamaʿa kaydahu in 54:44.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r2.anchor: فاجمعوا أبو عمرو ويعضده فجمع كيده

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r3.claim: Kayd means the means used to scheme.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r4.claim: They are to come arranged in a row; ṣaffan is a circumstantial accusative.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r4.anchor: مصطفين حال أمر وابان يأتوا صفا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r5.claim: Arriving in ranks is more fearsome to those watching.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r6.claim: The closing clause means whoever prevails today has succeeded and is parenthetical.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p60/r6.anchor: وقد فاز من غلب وهو اعتراض

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r9.claim: إجماع means making something firm and resolving upon it; one says أجمعت الخروج for resolving to depart.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r9.anchor: { فأجمعوا كيدكم } الإجماع الإحكام والعزم على الشيء. تقول: أجمعت الخروج وعلى الخروج أي عزمت.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r10.claim: All regional readers use فأجمعوا except Abū ʿAmr, who reads فاجمعوا with connected hamza and an open mīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r10.anchor: وقراءة كل الأمصار «فأجمعوا» إلا أبا عمرو فإنه قرأ «فاجمعوا» بالوصل وفتح الميم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r11.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r11.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, quoted by al-Naḥḥās, says Abū ʿAmr should read differently: since the preceding wording means gathered the plot, this form better means resolve.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r11.anchor: قال النحاس وفيما حكي لي عن محمد بن يزيد أنه قال: يجب على أبي عمرو أن يقرأ بخلاف قراءته هذه،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r12.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r12.claim: Al-Naḥḥās distinguishes the forms: after فجمع كيده, the resolve sense of فأجمعوا is more apt and different.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r12.anchor: قال: لأنه احتج ب«جمع» وقوله عز وجل: «فجمع كيده» قد ثبت هذا فيبعد أن يكون بعده «فاجمعوا»

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r13.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r13.claim: Al-Naḥḥās also accepts Abū ʿAmr's reading as gather every trick together; Abū Isḥāq agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r13.anchor: قال النحاس: ويصحح قراءة أبي عمرو «فاجمعوا» أي اجمعوا كل كيد لكم وكل حيلة فضموه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r14.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r14.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī says the hamza-cut, kasra reading can mean either gather or resolve and make firm.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r14.anchor: الثعلبي: القراءة بقطع الألف وكسر الميم لها وجهان: أحدهما: بمعنى الجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r15.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r15.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's verse uses نهب مجمع for gathered booty and supports the collection sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r15.anchor:
قال أبو ذؤيب يصف حمرا:
فكأنها بالجزع بين نبايع
وأولات ذي العرجاء نهب مجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r16.claim: إجماع means making something firm and resolving upon it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r16.anchor: { فأجمعوا كيدكم } الإجماع الإحكام والعزم على الشيء. تقول: أجمعت الخروج وعلى الخروج أي عزمت.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r17.speaker: author

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r19.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r19.claim: Al-Naḥḥās argues the following form should mean resolve, distinct from the previous gathering.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r19.anchor: قال: لأنه احتج ب«جمع» وقوله عز وجل: «فجمع كيده» قد ثبت هذا فيبعد أن يكون بعده «فاجمعوا»

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r20.anchor: قال النحاس: ويصحح قراءة أبي عمرو «فاجمعوا» أي اجمعوا كل كيد لكم وكل حيلة فضموه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:63-64/r21.anchor: الثعلبي: القراءة بقطع الألف وكسر الميم لها وجهان: أحدهما: بمعنى الجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r1.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r1.claim: A poet's phrase وأمري مجمع means my affair is firmly settled, supporting the resolve sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r1.anchor:
يا ليت شعري والمنى لا تنفع
هل أغدون يوما وأمري مجمع
أي محكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r2.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r2.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī take ثم ائتوا صفا to mean come together.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r2.anchor: { ثم ائتوا صفا } قال مقاتل والكلبي: جميعا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r3.claim: Another view takes صفا as rows, making the magicians more imposing.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda parses صفا as the object of ائتوا: come to the place where people assemble, the Eid prayer ground.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r4.anchor: وهو منصوب بوقوع الفعل عليه على قول أبي عبيدة قال يقال: أتيت الصف يعني المصلى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r5.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads the phrase as come while people are arrayed, with صفا a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial expression, hence singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يجوز أن يكون المعنى ثم ائتوا والناس مصطفون فيكون على هذا مصدرا في موضع الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r6.claim: A variant reads ثم ايتوا with yāʾ and kasra; when hamza is omitted it is replaced by alif.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r6.anchor: وقرىء «ثم ايتوا» بكسر الميم وياء. ومن ترك الهمز أبدل من الهمزة ألفا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r7.anchor: { وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى } أي من غلب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r8.claim: The words may be the magicians speaking to one another or Pharaoh addressing them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r8.anchor: وهذا كله من قول السحرة بعضهم لبعض. وقيل: من قول فرعون لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:64/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī

أي محكم.

QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r14.speaker: السحرة
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r14.claim: The sorcerers call on one another to unite their scheme and come in rows, claiming that the one who prevails that day will succeed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p265/r14.anchor: فأجمعوا كيدكم ثم ائتوا صفا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

STUDYQURAN:20:62/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:62/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:62/r1.claim: After Moses spoke, the sorcerers privately consulted on the best way to oppose and overcome him.
STUDYQURAN:20:62/r1.anchor: Upon hearing Moses’ words, the sorcerers consulted one another in private concerning the best means by which they could oppose and overcome him

TAB-FULL:v16p106/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p106/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p106/r1.claim: The one who prevails today succeeds by defeating his opponent.
TAB-FULL:v16p106/r1.anchor: قال: جمع فرعون الناس لذلك الجمع، ثم أمر السحرة فقال: {ائتوا صفا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى}

TAB-FULL:v16p106/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p106/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p106/r2.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih reports that Pharaoh gathered people and ordered the sorcerers to come in ranks, saying whoever prevails over his opponent succeeds.
TAB-FULL:v16p106/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: حدثت عن وهب بن منبه، قال: جمع فرعون الناس لذلك الجمع، ثم أمر السحرة فقال: {ائتوا صفا

TABATABAI:20:64/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r6.claim: Tanaazuʿ is close in meaning to disagreement and derives from pulling something from its place; it takes a direct object or may govern bi-fi.

TABATABAI:20:64/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r7.claim: Najwa means private speech; its original verbal-noun sense is speaking confidentially.
TABATABAI:20:64/r7.anchor: والنجوى الكلام الذي يسار به، وأصله مصدر

TABATABAI:20:64/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r10.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:20:64/r10.claim: Raghib defines ijmaʿ as collecting something after thought and deliberation.
TABATABAI:20:64/r10.anchor: على ما ذكره الراغب - جمع الشيء عن فكر وترو

TABATABAI:20:64/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r11.claim: Saff is arranging things in a straight line, such as people or trees; the word can function as a verbal noun or a result noun.
TABATABAI:20:64/r11.anchor: والصف جعل الأشياء على خط مستو كالإنسان والأشجار ونحو ذلك ويستعمل مصدرا واسم مصدر

TABATABAI:20:64/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r12.claim: The phrase may use saff as a verbal noun or mean “standing in ranks”; the command is to approach united and in agreement.
TABATABAI:20:64/r12.anchor: وأن يكون بمعنى صافين أي ائتوه باتحاد واتفاق من دون أن تختلفوا

TABATABAI:20:64/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r13.claim: They are urged to abandon division, marshal every stratagem, and meet Moses as one force so they can prevail.

TABATABAI:20:64/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:64/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:64/r14.claim: The dispute follows Moses’ preceding admonition, which affected some of them because it was a clear statement of truth: they lacked proof for their gods’ divinity or intercession.
TABATABAI:20:64/r14.anchor: ومن شأنها ذلك إذ ليست إلا كلمة حق ما فيها مغمض

TABATABAI:20:73/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r1.claim: The dispute seems first to have arisen among the magicians; the call to form ranks suggests some were hesitant or intended not to confront Moses.
TABATABAI:20:73/r1.anchor: أن الاختلاف إنما ظهر أول ما ظهر بين السحرة ومنهم

TABATABAI:20:73/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r2.claim: Pharaoh and his officials saw the people’s disagreement as humiliating, whispered privately, and ignored Moses’ wisdom and admonition.
TABATABAI:20:73/r2.anchor: أسروهم النجوى ولم يكلموهم فيما ألقاه إليهم موسى من الحكمة والموعظة

TABATABAI:20:73/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r3.claim: They shifted to accusing Moses of sorcery and alleging a political plan to expel the Egyptians from their land.
TABATABAI:20:73/r3.anchor: عدلوا عن ذلك إلى ما اتهمه فرعون بالسحر وطرح خطة سياسية لاخراج أمة القبط من أرضهم

TABATABAI:20:73/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r4.claim: The expulsion charge portrayed loss of homes and property and a fall from prosperity into misery, while the Israelites’ oppression was visible to them.
TABATABAI:20:73/r4.anchor: ففيه خروج من ديارهم وأموالهم وسقوط من أوج سعادتهم إلى حضيض الشقاء

TABATABAI:20:73/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r5.claim: Pharaoh added that abandoning the contest would destroy their inherited idolatrous national way of life, a custom bound up with their collective identity.
TABATABAI:20:73/r5.anchor: وأضافوا إلى ذلك أمرا آخر أمر من الجلاء والخروج من الديار والأموال وهو ذهاب طريقتهم المثلى وسنتهم القومية

TABATABAI:20:73/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r6.claim: The appeal exploits popular reverence for familiar national customs, which people often treat as sacred and heaven-given.
TABATABAI:20:73/r6.anchor: والعامة تقدس السنن القومية وخاصة ما اعتادت عليها وأذعنت بأنها سنن ظاهرة سماوية

TABATABAI:20:73/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r7.claim: This was political incitement, not a defense of true religion: Moses’ proof had exposed idolatry’s falsehood, but the regime presented it as the basis of its power and survival.
TABATABAI:20:73/r7.anchor: بل بعنوان أنها سنة ملية مقدسة تعتمد عليها مليتهم وتستند إليها شوكتهم

TABATABAI:20:73/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r8.claim: Their tactic was to unite, keep their customary order, and attack as one force, since division and Moses’ victory would mean their destruction.
TABATABAI:20:73/r8.anchor: فالرأي هو أن يجمعوا كل كيد لهم ثم يدعوا الاختلاف ويأتوا صفا حتى يستعلوا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

TABATABAI:20:73/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:73/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:73/r9.claim: Pharaoh reinforced the call for unity with attractive promises, as another passage shows.
TABATABAI:20:73/r9.anchor: وشفع ذلك فرعون بمواعد جميلة وعدهم إياها كما يظهر من قوله تعالى في موضع آخر

TABRISI:20:64-66/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:20:64-66/r5.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan distinguishes hamza forms: qatʿ for agreeing on something, waṣl with “gather your affair/plot”; most readers use qatʿ.
TABRISI:20:64-66/r5.anchor: قال أبو الحسن إنما يقولون بالقطع إذا قالوا إجمعوا على كذا فأما إذا قالوا أجمعوا أمركم وأجمعوا كيدكم فلا يقولون إلا بالوصل

TABRISI:20:64-66/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:20:64-66/r6.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan allows either a dialect variant in this sense or an analysis in which “agree on it” is followed by a new command about their plot.
TABRISI:20:64-66/r6.anchor: قال فأما أن يكون لغة في هذا المعنى لأن باب فعلت وأفعلت كثير

TABRISI:20:64-66/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66/r7.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:20:64-66/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī says this is not redundant with Pharaoh's earlier gathering of magic: that narrated Pharaoh, while this is the sorcerers' mutual instruction.
TABRISI:20:64-66/r7.anchor: قال أبوعلي: فإن قيل فقد تقدم ذكر قوله { فجمع كيده } فإذا قيل فأجمعوا كيدكم كان تكريرا

TABRISI:20:64-66/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66/r8.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:20:64-66/r8.claim: An unnamed poet uses “gather your affair” in the sense of “gather your plot.”
TABRISI:20:64-66/r8.anchor: وأنتم معشر زيدوا على مائة فأجمعوا أمركم طرا فكيدوني

TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r3.claim: The sorcerers are told to bring every bit of their stratagem to bear.
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r3.anchor: أي لا تدعوا من كيدكم شيئا إلا جئتم به

TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most commentators understand aligned ranks, giving their effort order and making it more intimidating.
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r4.anchor: أي مصطفين مجتمعين ليكون أنظم لأموركم وأشد لهيبتكم عن ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says ṣaff means the gathering place, the prayer ground where people assemble for the festival.
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: ثم ائتوا موضع الجمع ويسمى المصلى الصف عن أبي عبيدة

TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the saying as whoever prevails and rises above the other side has succeeded.
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r6.anchor: أي وقد سعد اليوم من غلب وعلا عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r7.claim: Some say Pharaoh said “whoever prevails today succeeds”; others attribute it to some magicians speaking to one another.
TABRISI:20:64-66#2/r7.anchor: إن هذا من قول فرعون للسحرة وقال آخرون بل هو قول بعض السحرة لبعض

TABRISI:20:74-76/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:74-76/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:74-76/r1.claim: An alternate attribution assigns “whoever prevails today succeeds” to the sorcerers.

THALABI:v6p252/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r1.claim: A second sense of ajmiʿū is to resolve and settle firmly: one says ajmaʿtu or azmaʿtu the matter, meaning that one resolved it.
THALABI:v6p252/r1.anchor: والثاني: بمعنى العزم والأحكام، يقول: أجمعت الأمر وأزمعته

THALABI:v6p252/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r2.claim: The magicians are to marshal and firmly plan their trick, deceit, magic, and expertise.
THALABI:v6p252/r2.anchor: وقد عزم عليه كيدكم ومكركم وسحركم وعلمكم

THALABI:v6p252/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r3.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
THALABI:v6p252/r3.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī take ṣaffan to mean that the magicians should come all together.

THALABI:v6p252/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r4.claim: Another explanation takes ṣaffan to mean in rows.

THALABI:v6p252/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v6p252/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says ṣaffan means the place of prayer or assembly; an eloquent Arab used “the ṣaff” to mean the prayer place.
THALABI:v6p252/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: يعني المصلى والمجتمع، وحكي عن بعض العرب الفصحاء

THALABI:v6p252/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r6.claim: The one who prevails today has succeeded.
THALABI:v6p252/r6.anchor: وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى يعني فاز من غلب

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r1.claim: The phrase means to gather or marshal your stratagems.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r2.claim: Ṣaffan can mean coming together as a group.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r2.anchor: ثم ائتوا صفا} أي جميعا. وقال أبو عبيدة: الصف: المصلى.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says al-ṣaff means a place of prayer.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الصف: المصلى. وحكى عن بعضهم أنه قال

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r4.claim: A speaker used “I could not come to the ṣaff today” to mean that he could not come to the prayer place.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p280#5/r4.anchor: وحكى عن بعضهم أنه قال: ما استطعت أن آتي الصف اليوم، أي المصلى (2) .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r1.claim: Al-Farra says ajmiʿū means to decide firmly, as in the construction “I resolved on the journey.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: (الإجماع: الإحكام والعزيمة على الشيء، تقول: أجمعت الخروج، وعلى الخروج، مثل: أزمعت، وأنشد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says all of them should unite in resolve and avoid disagreement in their stratagem.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (معناه: ليكن عزمكم كلكم على الكيد مجمعا لا تختلفوا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r3.claim: The author points to his discussion of the same sense of ijmāʿ at 10:71.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r3.anchor: ومضى الكلام معنى الإجماع عند قوله: {فأجمعوا أمركم} [يونس: 71].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r4.claim: Abu Amr reads fa-jmaʿū with connected hamza, from gathering, and cites Pharaoh’s gathering his stratagem at 20:60.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: فاجمعوا (¬6)، موصولا من الجمع، وحجته # قوله: {فجمع كيده} [طه: 60].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r5.claim: On the connected reading, al-Farra says they should bring every part of their stratagem and leave nothing unused.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: (معناه: فلا تدعوا من كيدكم شيئا إلا جئتم به)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise glosses it as bringing everything they can do and holding nothing back.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: (جيئوا بكل ما تقدرون عليه، ولا تبقوا منه شيئا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r7.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash prefers the connected reading, arguing that this wording is used for gathering, while the separated form is usual for resolving; he allows both as dialect forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r7.anchor: واختار الأخفش هذه القراءة وقال: (إنما يقولون بالقطع إذا قالوا: أجمعنا على كذا وكذا، فأما إذا قالوا: أجمعوا أمركم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r8.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r8.claim: Abu Ali says the two readings may reflect two dialects, as Abu al-Hasan suspected, and cites poetry using the separated form with “your affair.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي: (يشبه أن يكون ذلك على لغتين، كما ظنه أبو الحسن، كقول الشاعر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r9.speaker: الهذلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r9.claim: The Hudhali line uses mujmaʿ to mean “gathered,” supporting the gathering sense of the connected form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r9.anchor:
وقال الهذلي (¬6):
فكأنهما بالجزع بين نبايع ... وأولات ذي العرجاء نهب مجمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r10.claim: The verse tells the sorcerers to assemble all their magic and intensify it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p453/r10.anchor: وهذا فيما يتواصى به السحرة من جمع كيدهم، وما يستظهرون به من المبالغة في سحرهم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda says ṣaff can mean the gathering place, including a mosque or prayer ground, or can be a verbal noun meaning that people came lined up.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: (الصف: موضع الجمع، ويسمى المصلى: الصف، يقال: هل أتيت الصف اليوم؟ أي: المصلى الذي يصلى فيه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq gives two senses: come to the place of the festival prayer, or come together in ranks so their effort is orderly and their formation stronger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r2.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق الوجهين فقال: (معناه: ثم ائتوا الموضع الذي تجتمعون فيه لعيدكم وصلاتكم، يقال: أتيت صفا بمعنى أتيت المصلى،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r3.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي وابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r3.claim: The commentators, including Muqatil, al-Kalbi, and Ibn Abbas through ʿAta, gloss ṣaff as “all together,” meaning lined up.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r3.anchor: والمفسرون يقولون في قوله: {ثم ائتوا صفا}: (جميعا)، قاله مقاتل، والكلبي، وابن عباس في رواية عطاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that whoever prevails today has succeeded.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد قد سعد اليوم من غلب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r5.claim: Al-Layth says one who overcomes or rises above something may be described with istaʿlā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r5.anchor: قال الليث: (ويقال لكل من قهر أمرا أو علاه: اعتلا، واستعلاه واستعلى عليه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p455/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses istaʿlā as prevailing through victory.

MAJAZ:v2p22/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p22/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p22/r4.claim: Ṣaffan means rows; it can also mean a prayer place, as Abū al-ʿArab al-Kilābī’s remark about going to the ṣaff illustrates.
MAJAZ:v2p22/r4.anchor: ثم ائتوا صفا» (64) أي صفوفا وله موضع آخر من قولهم: هل أتيت الصف اليوم يعنى المصلى الذي يصلى فيه

NAHHAS:v3p46/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p46/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v3p46/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads فاجمعوا with hamzat al-waṣl and fatḥa on mīm, citing فجمع كيده ثم أتى.
NAHHAS:v3p46/r7.anchor: إلا أبا عمرو فإنه قرأ ( فاجمعوا ) بالوصل وفتح الميم

NAHHAS:v3p46/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p46/r8.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p46/r8.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd argues that Abū ʿAmr should use the other reading: since the earlier verse says they gathered their plot, this command more likely means resolve and prepare.
NAHHAS:v3p46/r8.anchor: قال يجب على أبي عمرو ومن بحجته أن يقرأ بخلاف قراءته هذه وهي القراءة التي عليها أكثر الناس

NAHHAS:v3p46/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p46/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p46/r9.claim: Abū Jaʿfar validates Abū ʿAmr's reading as gathering every plot and stratagem together with his brother.
NAHHAS:v3p46/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر تصحيح قراءة أبي عمرو فأجمعوا كل كيد وكل حيلة فضموه مع أخيه

NAHHAS:v3p46/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p46/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p46/r10.claim: صفا is accusative as the direct object of the verb.
NAHHAS:v3p46/r10.anchor: ( ثم أئتوا صفا ) منصوب بوقوع الفعل عليه

NAHHAS:v3p46/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p46/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v3p46/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says الصف can mean the prayer ground, so they are told to come to the place where people gather on Eid.
NAHHAS:v3p46/r11.anchor: وقول أبي عبيدة قال يقال أتيت الصف أي المصلى فالمعنى عنده أتوا الموضع الذي تجتمعون فيه يوم العيد

NAHHAS:v3p46/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p46/r12.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p46/r12.claim: Abū Isḥāq allows parsing صفا as a circumstantial qualifier.
NAHHAS:v3p46/r12.anchor: وزعم أبو إسحاق أنه يجوز أن يكون منصوبا على الحال

NAHHAS:v3p46/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p46/r13.speaker: هارون القارئ
NAHHAS:v3p46/r13.claim: Hārūn al-Qāriʾ identifies a dialect of Banu Tamim at this point, though the excerpt does not specify the form further.
NAHHAS:v3p46/r13.anchor: قال هارون القارىء لغة بني تميم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p385/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p385/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p385/r4.claim: The second sense is a gathered assembly or crowd, including those presented before their Lord and the magicians arriving together.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p385/r4.anchor: والثاني : الجمع . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف

THALABI:v6p251/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p251/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v6p251/r10.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads fājmaʿū with a connecting alif and fatḥa on mīm, meaning gather every scheme, as confirmed by the next verse.
THALABI:v6p251/r10.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو فاجمعوا بوصل الألف وفتح الميم، من الجمع يعني لا تدعوا شيئا من كيدكم

THALABI:v6p251/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p251/r11.speaker: الباقون
THALABI:v6p251/r11.claim: The other readers use a cut alif and kasra on mīm; one explanation gives it the same sense as gathering, since Arabs say both forms.
THALABI:v6p251/r11.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: فأجمعوا بقطع الألف وكسر الميم وله وجهان: أحدهما: بمعنى الجمع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r1.claim: They are told to settle on their plot without disagreement among themselves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r1.anchor: اعزموا على الكيد من غير اختلاف بينكم فيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r2.claim: They should come together in ordered ranks to make themselves more imposing.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r3.claim: The one who prevails today will prosper.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:64-69/r3.anchor: أي: قد سعد اليوم من غلب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r1.claim: Their stratagem is their magic, which they urge one another to assemble.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r1.anchor: قوله: {فأجمعوا كيدكم} [طه: 64] يعني: سحركم، يقوله بعضهم لبعض.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r2.claim: Coming in a row means coming together as a group.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r3.claim: Qatāda explains the successful one as the one who appears victorious.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r4.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses the successful one as the one who wins.

QASHANI:20:56-57/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:56-57/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:56-57/r9.claim: Imaginations precede intellect and certainty in human development; a caller to truth must first refute falsehood and doubt so truth can take hold.
QASHANI:20:56-57/r9.anchor: وإلقاؤها أولا إشارة إلى تقدم الوهميات والخياليات في الوجود الإنساني على العقليات واليقينيات عند السلوك

QASHANI:20:56-57/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:56-57/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:56-57/r10.claim: A caller to truth should first demolish falsehood and answer doubts with proof so false belief is removed and truth can settle.
QASHANI:20:56-57/r10.anchor: وإلى أن الواجب على الداعي إلى الحق أولا نقض الباطل ودفع الشبهة بالحجة

QASHANI:20:64-70/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:64-70/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:64-70/r1.claim: Pharaoh's people are told to coordinate their scheme and confront Moses and Aaron united in purpose.
QASHANI:20:64-70/r1.anchor: { فأجمعوا كيدكم } أي: اتفقوا فيما تبارزونهما به فتكونوا متفقي الكلمة متعاضدين

NASHR:v2p320/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p320/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p320/r7.claim: Abu Amr connects the hamza and opens the mīm in فأجمعوا كيدكم; the other readers cut the hamza and use kasra on mīm.
NASHR:v2p320/r7.anchor: فأجمعوا كيدكم فقرأ أبو عمر بوصل الهمزة وفتح الميم

DAMGHANI:v1p278/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p278/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p278/r17.claim: Ṣaff can mean a gathering; 18:48 likewise depicts people presented before their Lord gathered.
DAMGHANI:v1p278/r17.anchor: فوجه منها الصف الجمع قوله تعالى فى سورة طه ثم ائتوا صفا وقوله تعالى فى سورة الكهف وعرضوا على ربك صفا
